The moment after a printer is added is left to the model, and it changed every run
Same input, three runs, three different scripts. Run A: “creality k1” was saved at once and the reply ended with no offer to connect; the offer only appeared later, after I changed the nozzle. Run B: “Prusa MK4S” chosen from a chip was saved at once and nothing was offered at all. Run C (dark theme): the printer was saved and the offer came as bare “Yes / No” chips.

Run A: the K1 was saved from the name alone. The reply reads as a receipt, but nothing else marks the change and no next step is offered.
Run A: the K1 was saved from the name alone. The reply reads as a receipt, but nothing else marks the change and no next step is offered.
Run C: the same input, now with an offer and bare Yes / No chips. The second card is finding 06.
Run C: the same input, now with an offer and bare Yes / No chips. The second card is finding 06.
Why it matters. This is the one step every new user goes through, and it is the step that tells them the printer is ready. When the receipt line, the offer, and the chip labels are different each time, the product feels improvised, and a user who never sees the offer never learns that connecting exists.

Suggested change. Make the receipt deterministic. Either the app posts a fixed line and chip row when printer_add succeeds (“Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?” · Connect it · Not now), or the prompt names the exact chip text and requires the offer, with a live test that counts it across ten runs the way the nozzle rule was measured. Kenneth's decision that the assistant chooses the chips still holds if the prompt fixes the wording for this one moment.

bd8ea51abc Test printer connections across real profile changes and shell teardown
The shell harness called Orca's printer-agent switch directly, so it never
proved what a user's profile change does to a saved Bambu printer's
connection. It now selects profiles through Orca's own preset selection
and checks:

- selecting the printer's own Bambu profile keeps its connection;
- selecting a non-Bambu profile hands the connection software back to
  Orca's profile-driven choice, and the printer's status turns to
  "unknown" once the usual 30-second freshness window has passed (the
  same window that applies when a printer is switched off);
- connecting again reinstalls the Bambu connection software.

The default mode also checks that detaching the shell while a connection
agent the profile would not pick is installed restores the profile's
choice.

Printer setup verifies and saves a connection; it does not promise to
keep that connection active across later profile changes, which is the
stock Orca behavior these checks encode.

Verified on macOS RelWithDebInfo: --printer-setup 126/126, default
411/411 (three keyboard-focus checks skip themselves when the harness
window is not the active window).

8334b3395b Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives
The printer panel on Home was a three-phase flow with a different screen,
hard-coded buttons and one assistant tool per phase. It is now only a
conversation: the assistant adds, changes and connects printers through
eight tools, and every button the person taps is a reply the assistant
suggested ("Choices: a | b" as its last line, drawn as chips). The one card
left is printer_connect's, where an access code or API key is typed; it goes
straight to the connection and never into the conversation, the model's
requests, any note or the saved document.

- Tools: printer_identify, printer_add, printer_change,
  printer_connection_status, printer_connect, printer_manual_setup,
  printer_manual_connection, printer_setup_finish. Adding and changing run
  on the person's word: a new "confirmed in conversation" approval
  exemption, allowed only for printer panel tools. The connection tools act
  on the printer the conversation is about.
- The assistant acts on plain statements ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it") and
  asks only when it is guessing; naming a model adds it with the nozzle it
  ships with. A second add of the same model in one conversation is refused.
- A message sent while the credential card waits cancels the card, so a
  question such as "where is the access code?" gets its answer.
- Bambu Lab LAN only: discovery starts once per session, a printer's name
  is accepted as its device id, and the outcome of a connection reaches the
  model as a note. Connecting a printer that was already selected no longer
  fails with "The selected printer changed": the backend deselects it and
  selects it again one event turn later, after GUI_App's lost-connection
  notice has run.
- The panel always takes the whole window: Back, a menu with OrcaSlicer's
  printer list and printer settings, the thread and the composer. Removed:

  leave dialog, Home's "printer added" strip and the narrow side panel.

content.text:
No. The finding still holds on the current branch (`jusprin-newui` at bd8ea51abc). Nothing in the app posts a receipt or a "connect it?" offer when a printer is added. The model still writes that moment, and only a loose prompt rule guides it.

**What happens on a successful add**

- `PrinterConversation::add` ([PrinterConversation.cpp:401](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:401)) saves the printer, tells the host the printer list changed, and returns `{"printer": ...}` to the model. It adds no message, card or chip row to the conversation. By contrast, `printer_identify`, just above it, does push a block of printer cards.
- The only thing the app does itself is highlight the new printer's card on Home's printer list: a one-time CSS animation ([PrinterCard.tsx:21](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx:21), wired through [ShellController.cpp:254](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:254)). The printer panel fills the whole window, so I expect the person only sees that highlight after leaving the conversation. That is inference; I didn't run the app to confirm it.

**What the prompt says** ([printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts)). The line numbers in the finding still match this file.

- Line 33–35: after `printer_add`, "say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if theirs is different."
- Line 55: "Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once." It gives no wording and no chip labels. The general chip rule (lines 23–27) lets the model write its own labels, so bare "Yes / No" chips are allowed.

**Tests**

- The unit tests only check that the save happens and that a second add of the same model is refused.
- The live test, which runs the real model against a fake printer, doesn't count the offer. It opens the connect flow directly, and it only says "Yes, connect it" if the model hasn't already opened the card ([shell_harness.cpp:1052–1058](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:1052)). So a run where the model never offers to connect still passes.

The last commit to touch this area, 8334b3395b ("Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives"), removed Home's "printer added" strip. It didn't add anything in its place.

Both fixes the finding suggests are still open:
- **App-posted:** `add` pushes a fixed line and chip row, such as "Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?" with "Connect it" and "Not now".
- **Prompt-fixed:** the prompt names the exact wording and chips for this one moment, and a live check counts the offer over repeated runs.

I can start on either one.
I don't know what your question is, your response is extremely confusing.

Sorry, I buried the answer. Here it is plainly.

**No, nothing shows a receipt yet.** When a printer is added, the app saves it and hands the result to the assistant. After that, whatever appears in the chat is whatever the assistant decides to write. So the problem in the finding still exists: each run can word it differently, use different buttons, or skip the offer to connect.

The app itself adds only one thing: the new printer's card on Home flashes once. That flash is behind the printer panel, so the person likely won't see it until they leave the chat.

The recent commits didn't change this. One of them actually removed the old "printer added" banner on Home.

I'm not waiting on you for anything. If you want it fixed, the simplest option is for the app to post a fixed line with two buttons whenever a printer is added, such as "Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?" with "Connect it" and "Not now". Tell me if you want that and I'll build it.

What do you mean? Are you talking about hard coding the logics in the middle of the agent chat flow? If that's the case, how can we avoid the problems that we have done a lot of work to remove? Check reasoned commit for the problems that we put in a lot of effort to resolve.

Yes. The first fix I relayed from the finding, where the app posts a fixed line and fixed buttons after a successful add, would hard-code the chat flow. That is the kind of scripting the recent commits removed. I shouldn't have offered it as the simple option.

**What the recent commits removed, and why**

- **8334b3395b** ("Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives") replaced a three-step flow. That flow had its own screens, hard-coded "Add" and "Not this one" buttons, a success screen with a "Connect printer" button, and a "printer added" banner on Home. Now every button the person taps is a reply the assistant suggested. The only fixed card left is the one where an access code is typed, so the code never enters the chat.
- **a975c79be6** shows what the "printer added" banner cost. Its lifetime had to be fixed twice, because a second, blank refresh from the panel closing wiped it before anyone saw it. The same commit also fixed a hard-coded "Working on it..." line that only matched one of the two tools.
- **4d4f9e466b** removed a fixed summary card pinned above the chat, and moved that guidance into what the assistant says.

**What a fixed receipt in the chat would bring back.** This is my reasoning, not something I tested:

- **Two voices in one thread.** The assistant writes its own reply after the add, then the app adds its line. The person could get two receipts, or two that disagree.
- **Wrong in some cases.** Something like "Connect it over Wi-Fi?" is wrong if the person already said "add it and connect it". It is also wrong when the connection is by address rather than Bambu's LAN mode.
- **Buttons the assistant didn't write.** Tapping "Connect it" arrives as the person's message, replying to a question the assistant never asked.
- **Timing bugs.** The line has to land in the right place relative to the assistant's reply, which is the same kind of race the old banner had.

**What I'd do instead.** Keep the assistant in charge, and make this one moment consistent through the prompt and a test:

1. In [printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts), replace "after adding, offer it once" (line 55) with a specific requirement. Every reply to a successful add says which printer and nozzle were saved, then offers to connect, with suggested replies the assistant writes, such as "Connect it | Not now".
2. Add a check to the live test that counts across repeated runs whether that offer appears. The nozzle rule was measured the same way. Today the test still passes when the offer is missing.

That keeps your decision that the assistant writes the chips. Do you want me to make that prompt change and add the live check?

Yes. The chat already has a mechanism for exactly this, and it's how the printer candidate cards work today. One correction first: those cards no longer have an "Add this one" button. Commit 8334b3395b removed it. The person now answers the assistant's question, by tapping a suggested reply or typing, and the assistant calls `printer_add`.

**How the candidate cards work now**

1. When the assistant calls `printer_identify`, the app records a card entry in a list kept separately from the chat messages ([PrinterConversation.cpp:395](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:395)). Each entry has a kind (`"printers"`), the printers' names and pictures, and `afterMessageId`, the id of the chat message it follows.
2. The app sends that list to the chat page with the rest of the session state. The page draws each card right after its message ([MessageList.tsx:149](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx:149)). The type is defined in [protocol.ts:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:403), and its comment says no card has anything to tap.
3. **The list never reaches the model.** It is only read when the session state is sent to the page (line 268). The model learns what the cards show from the tool's own result, which carries the same printers as data.

So the cards are display-only and sit outside the model's history, which is what you're describing.

**A receipt built the same way**

- `PrinterConversation::add` adds an entry of a new kind, such as `"added"`, carrying the saved printer's name and nozzle. It uses the same code `identify` already uses.
- The page draws that kind as a receipt card.
- The model is unchanged: it still gets the `printer_add` result and writes its own reply.

I'd have the app create the card when the tool succeeds, not have the model write a tag like `<printer_added>` in its text. The app-created card appears only when the save really happened, in the same wording every time. A tag the model writes could be left out, misspelled, or written before the save succeeded. The page would also have to remove it from the text, and so would the chat history sent to the model.

**This avoids the earlier problems.** The receipt is a card, not a second chat message, so the thread still has one voice. Its buttons, if any, stay the assistant's. And its lifetime is the conversation's, not a separate refresh, which is how the old Home banner got wiped.

**What it doesn't fix:** the offer to connect. That is still the model's words, so it would still need the prompt change and the live test that counts it. The prompt should also tell the model the receipt card already shows what was saved, so it doesn't repeat it and just offers to connect.

Do you want me to build the receipt card this way?
Say what you're proposing in plain English in a language that a normal software engineer engineer can understand.

**The proposal:** when a printer is saved, show a small "printer added" card in the chat. The app draws it from the save itself, the AI never sees it, and the AI's text reply stays as it is.

**How it works**

- The chat window shows two kinds of things. There are chat messages, which are sent to the AI on every request. And there are display-only cards, which are stored in a separate list and never sent to the AI.
- The printer picture cards, the ones shown when the AI suggests which model you might have, are already display-only cards. Each card records which message it follows, and the chat window draws it there.
- I'd add one more card type, "printer added", with the printer's name and nozzle size. The app creates it in the same code that saves the printer, and only if the save succeeds.
- The chat window draws it as a receipt under the AI's reply.

**Why a card from the app, not a tag the AI writes:** the app knows for certain whether the save worked. If the AI wrote a tag like `<printer_added>`, it could forget it, get it wrong, or write it before the save actually happened. Every place that builds the AI's history would also have to strip it out.

**Why this doesn't bring back the old problems:** it isn't a scripted chat message. It has no buttons, and it doesn't change what the AI says or which reply suggestions it offers. It's a read-only card, like the picture cards already in the chat.

**What it doesn't solve:** whether the AI offers to connect the printer afterwards. That is still up to the AI. I'd handle it separately: tell the AI in its instructions that the card already shows what was saved, so it doesn't need to repeat it, and that it should always offer to connect next. Then add a test that runs the real AI several times and checks that the offer appears every time.
go ahead and build the receipt card as you suggested. Make sure you verify the results thoroughly to make sure the user experience is intuitive, as we intended

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. **What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

=== agent-panel-css-namespaces.md
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the

=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds.md
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

content.text:
The printer setup chat now shows a "Printer added" card when a printer is saved. It shows the printer's name and nozzle size, and the AI never sees it. It appeared correctly in every test run, including 7 runs against the real AI. One gap is left: the AI's own reply still says the printer was added, so the save is stated twice. My attempt to stop that broke the connect step, so I took it back out. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- When `printer_add` saves a printer, `PrinterConversation::add` records a display-only card, the same way the printer picture cards are recorded. The card goes under the chat message that asked for the save. If the save fails, or the same model is added again in one conversation, no card is added.
- The chat page draws it as a green check with "Printer added", then the name and nozzle, for example "Creality K1 · 0.4 mm nozzle". It has no buttons.
- The AI's instructions are unchanged.

I've attached screenshots in light and dark: naming a model, choosing one of three by tapping a suggested reply, and a long name in a narrow window. The narrow-window case showed a real problem: the long name cut the nozzle size off behind "…". I fixed it so the line wraps.

**Checks**
- **App-side unit tests:** all 247 pass. The new checks cover where the card goes, that there's no card after a failed or repeated add, and that the card never reaches the AI's history. They fail when the card code is removed.
- **Chat page tests:** all 190 pass. The design-token checks pass too.
- **Automated printer-setup and full test modes, without the AI:** 126 of 126 and 414 of 414.
- **Real AI, 7 runs:** exactly one receipt per add every time, and never a second one. Every run offered to connect afterwards.

**The instruction change I dropped**

I added a line telling the AI the card shows the save, so it shouldn't repeat it. The measured effect:

| | Connect step passed | AI still announced the save |
|---|---|---|
| With my line | 0 of 3 runs that reached it | 4 of 4 runs (shorter, mostly just "Added.") |
| Original instructions | 3 of 3 | Every run ("Your Bambu Lab A1 mini is set up with a 0.4 mm nozzle…") |

When connect failed, the AI invented a printer id and the app refused it. Once it told the person "I showed a card where you enter it" when no card was on screen. My guess is that a second thing called "a card" confused it with the access-code card, but I haven't proven that.

With the original instructions, the reply repeats what the card says. It isn't wrong, just redundant. Any new wording for that moment should be compared against the original over several live runs before it's used. Separately, the AI's buttons after an add were still sometimes a bare "Yes | No".

**Other things I found**
- One live run crashed. The AI closed the printer panel partway through the script, and the test script then sent a message to the closed panel. The crash is in the test script, not the app. I left a follow-up task for it.
- Some live-run failures appeared with both versions of the instructions, like the AI offering to open the full printer list instead of opening it. They are run-to-run variation in the AI, not something this change caused.

**Files changed:**
- [PrinterConversation.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp)
- [PrinterConversation.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.hpp)
- [protocol.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts)
- [PrinterPanel.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/PrinterPanel.tsx)
- [styles.css](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css)
- Tests: [test_printer_conversation.cpp](tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp), [PrinterPanel.test.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/PrinterPanel.test.tsx), [PrinterPanelApp.test.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/PrinterPanelApp.test.tsx), and [shell_harness.cpp](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp), which now checks for the receipt in live runs.

That notice is the watcher for an earlier comparison run timing out. That run finished before the summary above, and its results are already included there, so nothing needs to be done.
Is there anything I need to know besides the crash? Anything that didn't go as expected? Say that in plain English.

Yes, a few things. Most important first:

1. **The card fixes only half of the original problem.** Nothing in the chat marked a newly added printer; now the card does. But the AI's reply is still its own. It usually repeats what the card says, like "Your A1 mini is set up with a 0.4 mm nozzle", and it sometimes offers bare "Yes / No" buttons. My attempt to change that broke connecting, so I removed it.

2. **Changing the AI's instructions is riskier than it looks.** My one added line was about the moment after a printer is saved, and it made the later connect step fail every time (3 of 3 runs). With the original instructions, connect passed 3 of 3. Any future change to those instructions should be run live several times and compared against the original.

3. **The live test with the real AI doesn't pass reliably, even with no changes.** One of three runs with the original instructions failed an unrelated step, because the AI offered to open the full printer list instead of opening it. So one passing live run proves little, and the last commit's "104 of 104 passed" is probably one lucky run, not a stable result.

4. **I didn't see the card in the real app window.** My screenshots come from the built chat page, fed by a fake app I wrote, and I wrote the AI replies in them too. In the real-AI runs I confirmed the card from the app's data, not by looking at the screen. The page is the same, so I expect it to look identical, but I haven't seen it.

5. **One design call is yours.** When the AI adds a printer straight away, the printer picture card and the new receipt sit one on top of the other, and both name the printer. I thought that was fine, since the receipt's green check makes it read as a result, but you may want them merged.

6. **Left-over test folders may hold your API key.** There are many old `jusprin-shell-*` folders in the system temp directory. Each live test run leaves one behind, and it can contain the API key. I deleted the ones my runs created. I didn't delete the others because they came from other sessions, and one might still be running. Check that none are running, then clear them out.
By instructions, you mean the system prompt, right?

Yes. By "instructions" I meant the system prompt for the printer setup chat. It's written in [printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts) and sent to the model with every request in that chat.

The line I tried and then removed was:

> Once printer_add succeeds, the app shows a card under your message that says the printer was added and with which nozzle. Do not announce the save again or repeat its name and nozzle; go on to what comes next.

I had also removed an existing sentence: "Then say which nozzle it was set up with…". Both are back to how they were, so the file is identical to the last commit.
[Request interrupted by user]
Can you create a unit test to expose this problem?

Not in a way that would really expose the problem. The failure is a choice the live AI makes: with that line in the system prompt, it made up a printer id. Unit tests here don't call the AI. They use a scripted fake that gives the same answer whatever the prompt says, so no unit test can show that one prompt makes the AI behave worse than another.

Two things are possible:

1. **A unit test on the prompt text.** It would fail if the prompt ever calls anything a "card" other than the access-code card that connecting opens. It is fast, needs no AI, and would have caught my line. The catch: it encodes my guess about why connect broke, which I haven't proven. It could flag wording that is fine, or miss wording that breaks connect some other way.

2. **A repeated live test.** It runs just the connect conversation against the real AI five to ten times and reports how often the AI passes a printer id the app refuses. This is the check that actually exposes the problem: it failed 3 of 3 with my line and passed 3 of 3 without it. It costs API calls, takes a few minutes, and its result is a rate, not a pass or fail.

I'd build the second, since it measures the real behaviour, and add the first only if you want a cheap guard in the regular tests. Which do you want?

input.content:
---
name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: The live model invents Bambu deviceIds in ~20% of connect conversations even on the shipped prompt; a receipt-card prompt line roughly doubled that. Measure with --printer-connect-trials
metadata:
  type: project
---

Measured 2026-09-23/24 on branch claude/printer-receipt-card, with `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-connect-trials N`. The mode was added on that branch. It runs the connect conversation N times in fresh sessions against the fake Bambu printer, then prints HARNESS TRIAL and HARNESS TRIALS lines.

- **Shipped printer prompt:** reached the credential card in 15 of 19 connect conversations. In the rest, the model passed a made-up deviceId ("<from_status>", "JPN0001", "JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI_DEVICE_ID") and got unknown_device.
- **With a line about the "Printer added" receipt card** ("the app shows a card under your message… Do not announce the save again"): reached the card in 5 of 13, with ids such as "1", "deviceId" and "A1M-001".
- Combined, a two-sided Fisher test gives p≈0.03. The 10-vs-10 set alone gives p≈0.35.

An earlier 0/3 vs 3/3 result was over-read as "the line breaks connect; without it connect works". That was wrong: the shipped prompt fails too. It also explains the flaky live_connect_asks_for_the_code_on_its_card failures in --printer-live.

**Why:** a single full --printer-live run is one sample of a stochastic model. Small A/Bs mislead in both directions.

**How to apply:** judge any printer-prompt change with --printer-connect-trials, at least 10 runs per arm, comparing counts. The deviceId invention on the shipped prompt is a real, open product issue. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

The repeated live test is built, and it shows the problem is bigger than I said. The AI makes up printer ids when connecting even with the current system prompt, about one conversation in five. My removed line made it worse, but it wasn't the only cause.

**What the test does.** It's a new mode in the test app, `--printer-connect-trials N`. It saves a Bambu Lab A1 mini without involving the AI and turns on the built-in fake Bambu printer. Then it runs the "connect this printer" conversation with the real AI N times, each in a fresh chat. For each attempt it prints whether the AI got to the access-code card, and any printer id the app refused. At the end it prints the totals. It passes only if every attempt reaches the card, unless you set a lower bar with `--trials-must-reach`.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=... build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-connect-trials 10
```

**Results** (all samples = these 10-attempt sets plus the earlier runs):

| System prompt | Reached the card, 10 attempts | All samples |
|---|---|---|
| Current, unchanged | 8 of 10 | 15 of 19 (79%) |
| With my removed line put back | 5 of 10 | 5 of 13 (38%) |

When it fails, the AI sends a made-up id instead of the real one ("FAKE001"). Examples with the current prompt: "<from_status>" and "JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI_DEVICE_ID". With my line: "1", "deviceId" and "bambu-a1mini-1".

**What this changes from what I told you before:**
- I said the connect failures came from my line and that the current prompt was fine. That was wrong. It rested on 3 runs per side, and the current prompt fails too. This also explains why the full live test has been failing its connect step on and off.
- My line probably does make it worse. Across all samples the gap is unlikely to be chance (about 3%), but the 10-against-10 comparison alone isn't conclusive. Keeping it out was still the right call.
- A real person hitting this sees the assistant fail to open the access-code card. Fixing that is a separate piece of work, and this test is how to check a fix.

**Something that went wrong while building it:** the first version miscounted. Every new chat numbers its tool calls from 1 again, so the test treated later attempts' calls as already seen, and three real successes were counted as failures. I found it by reading each attempt's log, fixed it, and all the results above come from the fixed version.

**Where things are.** Everything is on branch `claude/printer-receipt-card`, in the worktree at `.claude/worktrees/printer-receipt-card`: the "Printer added" card, its tests, and this new mode. The main checkout is clean again. The system prompt file there matches the last commit; the A/B script swapped my line in and restored the file afterwards. Nothing is committed. I deleted the test data folders my runs created, since they held the API key. I also corrected the note I had saved earlier, which blamed my line alone.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Printer panel conversations against the live model, without the app.

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt (printerInstructions.ts),
eight printer tools and the chat. This script sends the model the same
requests the app sends, answers the tools the way the app answers them for a
fixed printer, and checks what the model does. A case is a short scripted
conversation; each run of it is one sample of a model that answers
differently each time, so a case is run many times and the result is a count.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from printerInstructions.ts by render_prompt.mjs,
    so an edit to the prompt is tested without building anything;
  - tools: printer_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the printer panel
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: earlier turns as plain text only -- the app keeps no tool calls or
    tool results between turns -- then this turn's message, then this turn's
    tool calls and their results (OpenAIResponsesAgent, AgentHost).
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs.

Usage:
  OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py [--runs 10]
      [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--model gpt-5.4-mini] [--verbose]

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs
(default: all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's
npm install (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses")
MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini"  # OpenAIResponsesConfig's default model
TOOLS = json.loads((HERE / "printer_tools.json").read_text())
MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN = 8


def render(session):
    """The page's system prompt and opening line for this session."""
    node = shutil.which("node")
    if node is None:
        sys.exit("node is required to render the printer panel's prompt")
    result = subprocess.run([node, str(HERE / "render_prompt.mjs")], input=json.dumps(session),
                            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return json.loads(result.stdout)


def post(body, key):
    request = urllib.request.Request(ENDPOINT, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
                                     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
                return json.load(response)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            if error.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503) or attempt == 4:
                raise RuntimeError(f"OpenAI {error.code}: {error.read().decode(errors='replace')[:500]}")
        except urllib.error.URLError:
            if attempt == 4:
                raise
        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)


def output_text(item):
    return "".join(part.get("text", "") for part in item.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "output_text")


def invalid_arguments(tool, arguments):
    """The registry's check before a tool runs, as far as the schema says."""
    schema = next((t["parameters"] for t in TOOLS if t["name"] == tool), None)
    if schema is None:
        return {"code": "unknown_tool", "message": f'There is no tool named "{tool}" here. Nothing was proposed. Use one of the listed tools.'}
    missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in arguments]
    extra = [name for name in arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
    if missing or extra:
        return {"code": "invalid_arguments",
                "message": f"Missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}. Nothing was proposed. "
                           "Check the arguments against this tool's parameters and call it again."}
    return None


class Conversation:
    """One run of a case: the chat as the app would hold it."""

    def __init__(self, case, prompt, key, model):
        self.case, self.instructions, self.key, self.model = case, prompt["instructions"], key, model
        self.history = [{"role": "assistant", "content": prompt["opening"]}]  # the page's opening line
        self.log = ["assistant: " + prompt["opening"]]
        self.done = False

    def say(self, words):
        """One turn: the person's words, then the model until it stops or a card waits."""
        self.log.append("person: " + words)
        turn = self.history + [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": words}]}]
        replies = []
        rejected = 0
        for _ in range(MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN):
            response = post({"model": self.model, "store": False, "parallel_tool_calls": False,
                             "instructions": self.instructions, "tools": TOOLS, "input": turn}, self.key)
            output = response.get("output", [])
            turn += output
            replies += [output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message" and output_text(item)]
            call = next((item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"), None)
            if call is None:
                break
            arguments = json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
            self.log.append(f"tool: {call['name']} {json.dumps(arguments)}")
            problem = invalid_arguments(call["name"], arguments)
            if problem and rejected < 2:
                rejected += 1
                result, waits = {"state": "failed", "error": problem}, False
            else:
                result, waits = self.case.tool(call["name"], arguments)
            self.log.append("  -> " + json.dumps(result))
            if waits:
                break  # a card is up: the app waits for the person
            turn.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": json.dumps(result)})
        # Between turns the app keeps only the words.
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": words})
        for reply in replies:
            self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
            self.log.append("assistant: " + reply)


# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------


class ConnectBambu:
    """Connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network in LAN mode.

    Passes when the model opens printer_connect's card for that printer. The
    person confirms twice at most, as --printer-live's script does.
    """

    name = "connect-bambu"
    session = {
        "mode": "connect", "printerName": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "blocks": [],
        "context": {"printer": {
            "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "model": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.4, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
            "spools": [{"name": "Teal PLA", "material": "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M", "colour": "#26A69A"}],
            "connected": False, "provider": "bambu"}},
    }
    # printer_connection_status as the app answered it for the fake printer.
    status = {"address": "", "candidates": [{"address": "127.0.0.1", "deviceId": "FAKE001", "name": "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"}],
              "hostType": "", "message": "", "nozzleMismatch": False, "provider": "bambu", "state": "not_configured"}

    def __init__(self):
        self.card = False
        self.refused = []
        self.other = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        if name == "printer_connection_status":
            return self.status, False
        if name == "printer_connect":
            # The app accepts a listed printer's id or its name (preflight_tool).
            device = arguments.get("deviceId", "")
            if device in ("FAKE001", "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"):
                self.card = True
                return {"state": "pending"}, True
            self.refused.append(device)
            return {"error": {"code": "unknown_device",
                              "message": "Pass the deviceId of one of these printers in LAN mode: FAKE001 (JusPrin Fake A1 mini)."}}, False
        self.other.append(name)
        if name == "printer_manual_connection":
            return {"state": "opened"}, False
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

    def run(self, conversation):
        conversation.say("Yes, it is")
        if not self.card:
            conversation.say("Yes, connect it")
        detail = "card" if self.card else "NO CARD"
        if self.refused:
            detail += "; refused " + ", ".join(repr(device) for device in self.refused)
        if self.other:
            detail += "; also called " + ", ".join(self.other)
        return self.card, detail


CASES = {case.name: case for case in (ConnectBambu,)}


# --- Runner ------------------------------------------------------------------


def run_once(case_class, prompt, key, model):
    case = case_class()
    conversation = Conversation(case, prompt, key, model)
    try:
        passed, detail = case.run(conversation)
    except Exception as error:  # a failed request is a failed run, reported as such
        passed, detail = False, f"ERROR {error}"
    return passed, detail, conversation.log


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", choices=sorted(CASES), help="run only this case (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=10, help="runs per case (default 10)")
    parser.add_argument("--must-pass", type=int, help="runs per case that must pass (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=5, help="runs in parallel (default 5)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every run's conversation, not only failures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        sys.exit("OPENAI_API_KEY is required")
    must_pass = args.runs if args.must_pass is None else args.must_pass

    ok = True
    for name in args.case or sorted(CASES):
        case_class = CASES[name]
        prompt = render(case_class.session)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda _: run_once(case_class, prompt, key, args.model), range(args.runs)))
        passed = sum(1 for result in results if result[0])
        for index, (good, detail, log) in enumerate(results, 1):
            print(f"{name} run {index}/{args.runs}: {detail}")
            if args.verbose or not good:
                for line in log:
                    print("    " + line.replace("\n", "\n    "))
        print(f"{name}: {passed} of {args.runs} passed (needs {must_pass})")
        ok = ok and passed >= must_pass
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Printer panel prompt tests

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), eight printer
tools, and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same
requests the app sends. It answers the tools the way the app answers them for
a fixed printer, then checks what the model did. The app does not run.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --runs 20
```

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case
runs many times, in parallel, and reports a count. 20 runs take about 20
seconds. By default every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.
`--verbose` prints every conversation, not only the failed ones.

## Judging a prompt change

Run the cases before and after the edit and compare the counts. The script
renders the prompt from the TypeScript source on every run, so nothing needs
building. Differences of a few runs out of 20 are noise; look for a clear gap.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt and the opening line** come from the page's own source,
  through `render_prompt.mjs` and the page's esbuild. This needs node and the
  AgentUI npm install.
- **`printer_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the printer panel.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it drifts from the registry.
  Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[printer]'`.
- **The chat history** is built the way `AgentHost` and `OpenAIResponsesAgent`
  build it: earlier turns as plain text only, with no tool calls or tool
  results; then this turn's message, tool calls and results.
- **Tool answers** are what the app returned for the in-process fake Bambu
  printer, recorded from a real run.

The app streams its requests and this script does not; nothing else differs.

## Cases

- `connect-bambu`: connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network.
  Passes when the model opens `printer_connect`'s card for it. It fails often
  today. The model looks up the printer's id in one turn, and the app drops
  that tool result before the next turn. When the person then says "connect
  it", the model has no id and invents one, such as `<from_status>`.

A new case is a class in `run_prompt_tests.py` that has a session payload, a
`tool()` that answers calls, and a `run()` that says the person's lines and
returns the outcome. Add it to `CASES`.

name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: Bambu connect fails ~30% because the app drops tool results between turns, so the model invents deviceIds; tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py measures prompt changes in seconds without the app
metadata:
  type: project
---

Found 2026-09-24 on branch claude/printer-receipt-card, by recording the app's OpenAI requests through a local proxy (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`).

**The root cause.** Between turns, AgentHost sends only the messages' text. It sends no function calls and no function_call_outputs. In turn 1 the model calls printer_connection_status and learns `deviceId: FAKE001`, then says "I found one A1 mini". On "Yes, connect it" that result is gone, so a model that calls printer_connect without checking again invents an id (`<from_status>`, `A1 mini`, `<deviceId from printer_connection_status>`) and gets unknown_device. Unfixed when this memory was written. Candidate fixes: put the discovered candidates in the connect session's context, or keep a session's tool results across turns.

**Rates**, from `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (connect-bambu):
- Shipped prompt: about 64% (32 of 50).
- With a prompt line about the "Printer added" receipt card: 4 of 20.

The app-based runs agreed in direction. That line stays out.

**The lightweight test:** run_prompt_tests.py uses only Python's stdlib plus node. It renders the prompt from printerInstructions.ts via render_prompt.mjs, sends printer_tools.json (guarded by a test in test_openai_responses_agent.cpp; regenerate with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1), and copies the text-only history. 20 runs take about 20 s. The shell harness's --printer-connect-trials mode was built, then removed in favour of it.

**Why:** single app runs are single samples. 0/3 vs 3/3 was once over-read as "the shipped prompt works".

**How to apply:** judge printer prompt edits with run_prompt_tests.py, 20 or more runs per side. Add new cases there, not to the shell harness. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

The system prompt test is now a small Python script that doesn't need the app. It runs 20 conversations with the real model in about 20 seconds, where the app-based version took about 20 minutes. It needs only Python's standard library and Node, which the chat page's build already uses. Building it also found the real cause of the connect failures, which is in the app, not the system prompt.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --runs 20
```

**Why the model makes up printer ids.** Between turns, the app sends the model only the words of the chat, not its earlier tool calls or their results. The model looks up the printer's real id in one turn and says "I found one A1 mini". When the person then says "Yes, connect it", the id is no longer in what the model receives. If the model doesn't look it up again, it invents one, such as "<from_status>". I confirmed this by recording the exact requests the app sends to OpenAI. It is not fixed yet.

**How the script stays faithful to the app**
- **System prompt and opening line:** built from the real TypeScript source on every run, so an edit to the prompt is tested with no build. The output is byte-for-byte identical to what the app sent.
- **Tool definitions:** in `printer_tools.json`, an exact copy of what the app sends. A new C++ unit test fails if the copy ever drifts from the app; I confirmed it fails when the file is changed. `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1` regenerates the file.
- **Chat history:** built the way the app builds it, text only between turns. That is the behaviour that causes the bug, so the script reproduces it.
- **Tool answers:** the answers the real app gave for its built-in fake Bambu printer.
- **One difference:** the app streams its requests and the script doesn't. That doesn't change what the model sends back.

**Results for connecting a Bambu printer**

| System prompt | Passed |
|---|---|
| Current | 32 of 50 (64%) |
| With my removed receipt line | 4 of 20 |

The failures look exactly like the app's. So the line I removed really did hurt, and the current prompt fails about a third of the time on its own. The script exits with failure by default; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.

**Other changes**
- I removed the `--printer-connect-trials` mode from the test app, since the script replaces it. The test app keeps only its receipt checks.
- All 248 unit tests pass.
- Nothing is committed. The work is on branch `claude/printer-receipt-card`, and the new files are in `tests/printer_prompt/`: the script, the prompt renderer, the tools file and a README.

**Next decision: fixing the connect bug.** The script can measure either fix in seconds:
1. **Put the printers found on the network into the connect chat's system prompt** (my recommendation). The app already does this when adding a printer, so it's a small change inside the fork's own code.
2. **Keep the printer chat's tool results in the history between turns.** This is broader, and it changes shared agent code that the project chat also uses.

Want me to try the first fix and measure it?
how did you make sure .claude/worktrees/printer-receipt-card/tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py sends exactly the same system prompt as the live code?

Two ways, and one of them was only a one-time check.

**1. The script has no copy of the system prompt.** It runs the chat page's own source. [render_prompt.mjs](tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs) compiles the real `printerInstructions.ts` and `printerWords.ts` with the page's own esbuild, then calls the same `printerInstructions(session)` and `opening(session)` functions the page calls. A change to the TypeScript reaches the script on its next run.

**2. I compared the output against the real app once.** I ran the test app with its OpenAI address pointed at a small local proxy that saved every request (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8791/...`). Then I fed the script's renderer the same printer and compared its output to the `instructions` field the app had sent. The result:

```
instructions identical: True
opening identical: True
```

**What isn't guaranteed.** The system prompt is built from two inputs: the TypeScript, and the facts the app supplies about the printer. The script shares the TypeScript. The printer facts (name, nozzle, spools, "Connects through: Bambu Lab LAN mode" and so on) are typed by hand into the `ConnectBambu` case, copied from that one recording.

Nothing checks those facts stay right. If the app changes what it sends, say a new field or a different nozzle list, the script would keep sending the old version and nothing would fail. The byte-for-byte match was also checked only once, by me, not by a test that runs again.

The fix is a small guard like the one for the tool list: a unit test that builds the app's printer facts for a Bambu A1 mini and fails if they differ from the script's copy. Want me to add it?

content.text:
The test is committed, and the experiment answers the question. The prompt change didn't really change how the model connects. It changed whether the model happens to repeat the printer's name in a harmless sentence one turn earlier, and because of the chat-history bug, that sentence is the only thing carrying the printer's id forward.

**Commit.** `52be072920` "Test the printer panel's system prompt against the live model without the app", on branch `claude/printer-receipt-card`. It has only the test files and the C++ check on the tools file. The "Printer added" card work is still uncommitted beside it.

**How the experiment worked.** I split my earlier change into its parts: the sentence it removed, the line it added, and each clause of that line on its own. I also added two neutral sentences about spool colours and build volume as controls. I ran each version 60 to 90 times through the new test (about 660 conversations, a few minutes). For each run I recorded three things:
- Did the first reply name the printer?
- Did the model look the printer up again on "connect it"?
- Which id did it pass?

**What decides success**

| After the model found the printer, its first reply… | …and on "connect it" | Passed |
|---|---|---|
| quoted its name, "JusPrin Fake A1 mini" | — | about 87% |
| left the name out | looked it up again | 100% (rare) |
| left the name out | didn't look again | 0 of 129 |

- The model almost never looks the printer up again. Its only link to the printer is its own earlier sentence.
- If that sentence quotes the name, the model can pass the name, and the app accepts a name as an id.
- The failures among named runs came from the model rebuilding an id from the name, like "JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI", instead of copying it exactly.

**How much each version changed it**

| System prompt | Named the printer | Passed |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 83% | 71% |
| Neutral sentence about spool colours | 59% | 59% |
| Neutral sentence about build volume | 62% | 63% |
| Only the receipt line added | 38% | 41% |
| Full receipt change | 19% | 32% |

**Why a small change had a big effect.** The outcome rides on a stylistic choice: whether to write "I found one A1 mini" or "I found JusPrin Fake A1 mini". Nothing in the system prompt asks for either, so almost any edit moves it. Even the unrelated neutral sentences pushed it down, though each on its own was within chance (p = 0.12 and 0.37). The receipt line pushed it much further (p < 0.001 against the current prompt, and 0.0005 against the neutral control). The full change pushed it furthest.

**What I couldn't settle.** Which words in the receipt line did the damage. "Do not repeat its name" looks like the obvious suspect, but tested alone it didn't reduce naming (26 of 30 runs named the printer). The large drop showed up only in combinations, and I haven't untangled those.

**What this means.**
- The prompt isn't the real problem. As long as the app drops the looked-up id between turns, the connect success rate depends on incidental wording, and every future prompt edit risks it.
- If the app put the printers it found on the network into the connect chat's context, the model wouldn't need its own sentence to remember the id. I'd expect both the failure rate and this sensitivity to mostly disappear, and the same test can check that quickly.

content.text:
The instruction change is gone: the system prompt file matches the last commit. I ran the live test with the real model and it passed every check. The six screenshots above are real conversations from those runs. In every run the receipt appeared after each printer was added, and a second "yes, add it" produced no second receipt. The remaining inconsistency is in what the model says next, not in the card.

**How the screenshots were made.** This Mac refuses screen capture, so the test app can't photograph its own window. Instead, the live test saved the exact page state the app sent the chat page at each moment. I then loaded that into the same built chat page in a browser and took the screenshots. The words and cards are the real model's and the app's; only the rendering happened in a browser. To support this, I added a capture option to the live test (`PRINTER_LIVE_CAPTURE_DIR`). The live test also has a new step for a tapped answer: after "prusa mk4", it answers "Prusa MK4S".

**What the screenshots show**

1. **Typing a model:** "the A1 mini" shows the printer's picture, then "✓ Printer added · Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4 mm nozzle", then the model's reply: "Your Bambu Lab A1 mini is set up with a 0.4 mm nozzle…". The reply repeats the card, which you said is fine.
2. **Saying yes a second time:** no second receipt. The model replies that it was already added.
3. **Choosing one of three:** "prusa mk4" shows three picture cards and suggested replies. Choosing "Prusa MK4S" adds it with its receipt. In the light and dark screenshots of this, the opening line is only scrolled out of view.

**What you may not like**

- **The offer to connect still varies.** In one A1 mini run the model didn't offer to connect at all. For the MK4S it offered in passing ("I can also help connect it to the network next") with no suggested replies. That's the other half of your original finding, and the card doesn't address it.
- **The picture appears twice after choosing from a list.** The model looks up the chosen printer again, so a large MK4S picture card sits right above the receipt, after the same printer already appeared in the list of three.

**Where things stand.** Nothing new is committed. The receipt card and the live test's capture option are uncommitted on branch `claude/printer-receipt-card`, next to the committed prompt test. Tell me if the result is good enough and I'll commit them.

I think you got the user experience wrong, and I suspect this is why your test case behave very strange. The more natural user experience is:

* agent gives init info
* user provides input/photo
* agent checks against tool.
* if only 1 found, shows printer cards. agent asks "should I add this one?" + yes/not chips
* if up to 3 found, shows printer cards. agent asks "which one?"  + printer chips + none of them chip
* if more than 3 or 0, agent flllows up.
* if users clicks positive chip, add "yes confirmed" (or something more clear) as user msg. agent calls tool to add it. tool returns success. we should printer added card. agent can repeat the card and it's ok
* in agent's response, Either with or without repeating the printer added info, further prompt for connecting the printer. 

Do you think this is a more natural user experience? if so, is this something you can achieve with the instructions? Or you think that this will be too complicated for agent to follow reliably?

Yes, I think your flow is more natural, and simpler for the model than today's. I expect instructions can get most of it right, with two small app changes where instructions alone are weakest. That's my judgement, not measured yet; the new prompt test can measure it before anything ships.

**Why it's better.** Today the system prompt tells the model to add a printer as soon as someone names it plainly, and to ask first only when it's guessing. That's two paths, and the model has to decide which applies. Your flow has one path: always show the cards, always ask, save only after a yes. The confirmation also catches a wrong match before anything is saved.

**One correction.** The strange connect failures in the tests don't come from the add flow. They come from the app dropping tool results between turns, which is separate from how adding works.

**What instructions can do reliably.** Models copy exact wording far more consistently than they follow general rules. The finding's "Yes / No" chips came from the prompt saying only "two to four short answers". So the prompt should spell out each moment's exact words and chips:
- One match: "Is this your printer?" with **Yes, add it** · **No, a different one**.
- Two or three: "Which one is yours?" with one chip per printer plus **None of these**.
- More than three, or none: ask one narrowing question, or offer the full list, with no cards.
- After the add: the reply ends with "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and **Connect it** · **Not now**.

Tapping a chip already sends its text as the person's message, so a clear label like "Yes, add it" is the confirmation.

**Where I'd help the model from the app instead:**
- **The connect offer.** Right after the add, the model reads the `printer_add` result, so the app can put the next step there. It would be a line in the tool's result saying to offer connecting, with those two chips. That's more reliable than a rule written far away in the system prompt.
- **The dropped tool results.** Your flow crosses a turn boundary between "here's the card" and "yes, add it". Adding still works, because the printer list with its ids is in the system prompt. But the same boundary is what breaks connecting, and it would also let the model call `printer_identify` again after "Yes, add it", which is the duplicate picture card in the MK4S screenshot. Fixing how the history is built, or putting the found printers into the connect chat's context, removes that fragility for every step.

**How I'd find out whether it's reliable enough.** Add a case to the prompt test for each step before changing the app:
- one match: asks, adds nothing, uses the exact chips;
- three matches: printer chips plus "None of these";
- "Yes, add it": calls `printer_add` without calling `printer_identify` again;
- after the add: the connect offer and its chips appear.

Run each 30 times against the new system prompt. If every step is at or near 30 of 30, instructions are enough. Any step that isn't shows exactly where the app has to take over.

Want me to write the new prompt and those cases and measure them?

# Handoff: the model now sees each chat's earlier tool calls and results

Written 2026-09-24 by the session "Tool calls/results in LLM message history".
Untracked on purpose: read it from this path, do not commit it.

## What changed

Commit `115e2776bf` on `jusprin-newui` ("Replay each chat's earlier tool calls
and results to the model"). Before it, between turns the app sent the model only
the text of earlier messages. Now every chat, printer panel and project alike,
replays each earlier assistant message's tool calls with their results, in the
order they were made. There is no per-session switch: a first version had one
(printer on, project off); Kenneth asked what scenario needs it off, there was
none, and he had it removed.

The pieces, all inside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`:

- `Agent/ToolExecution.hpp`: `ToolActivity::call_id`, the provider's id for the
  call. Saved in the project document as `callId`
  (`Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp`). Empty for MCP-sourced activities and for
  records written before this commit; those are not replayed.
- `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.hpp`: `propose(...)` takes the call id as a
  trailing argument; `AgentHost::handle_agent_tool_call` passes it.
- `Agent/AgentService.hpp`: `AgentConversationContext` gained `call_id`, `tool`,
  `arguments_json`, `output_json`. One entry per call+result pair (role and text
  empty), so the 20-entry history cap in `AgentHost::make_agent_request` can
  never send a call without its output. The cap now counts entries: a replayed
  call counts as one, like a message.
- `Agent/AgentHost.cpp`: `make_agent_request` groups the document's activities
  by `correlation_id` (the assistant message that made the call) and emits them
  right after that message's text, before the follow-up reply. An assistant
  message with empty text (it only called a tool) still contributes its calls.
  `tool_output_json(activity)` builds what the model reads, shared with the live
  path (`continue_after_tool`): state, result, error, then the session's own
  formatter (`PrinterConversation::tool_output`) if it has one. On replay the
  live result's `actionId`, `workspaceRevision` and `workspace` are left out:
  the turn carries the current workspace. A replayed result over 16 KiB is sent
  as `{"state": ..., "omitted": "The result, N bytes, is not repeated here; call
  the tool again for it."}`.
- `Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp`: `initial_input` emits each pair as a
  `function_call` (`call_id`, `name`, `arguments`) followed by a
  `function_call_output` (`call_id`, `output`). The response's item `id`
  (`fc_...`) is deliberately not sent: with `store:false` it names nothing the
  service kept, and other projects hit errors replaying it. Within a turn the
  adapter still keeps the full input as before; nothing changed there.

Tests (all in `tests/agent/`, target `agent_bridge_tests`, 255 cases pass):

- `test_printer_conversation.cpp`: "a session replays its earlier tool calls to
  the model, printer or project" (printer section: replayed output equals the
  live one byte for byte and sits between the question and the reply; project
  section: result equal, workspace and actionId absent) and "a large earlier
  result is replayed as its state and a note, not its bytes".
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`: "OpenAI request replays an earlier turn's
  call beside its output, with no item id" checks the exact wire fields.
- `test_project_state.cpp`: `callId` survives save and reload.

## What was measured

Live, against `gpt-5.4-mini` with the printer session's real tools and rendered
system prompt, 5 runs per arm. Turn 1 "is it online?" (the app runs
`printer_connection_status`, which lists `deviceId 01P00A3B`, name Workshop),
turn 2 "Yes, connect it":

| History sent | Correct `printer_connect` | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text only (before) | 0 of 5 | 2 sent `hostType: moonraker` for a Bambu printer, 1 passed the name as the id, 2 looked again |
| With the replayed call | 5 of 5 | none |

This also shows the OpenAI service accepts the replayed shape. The project chat
was NOT measured live.

How to repeat in about 30 s without the app (recipe also in memory):
1. `PRINTER_EVAL_OUT=<dir> agent_bridge_tests "[.printer-eval]"` writes the real
   request (tools, model, store) and session state.
2. Render the real prompt: bundle a 4-line TS that calls
